Limits of sums and products

Source: R/concrete-limits.R
sum-limits.Rd

sum_index(s, x) is the position of the index x among the limits of a Sum or Product (from 0, as SymPy's index). reorder_limit(s, i, j) swaps two limits and sym_reorder(s, ...) (SymPy's reorder) applies swaps given as pairs of positions or indices. change_index(s, var, trafo, newvar) substitutes a linear transformation of an index. reverse_order(s, ...) reverses the limits at the given positions or indices (Karr's convention). euler_maclaurin(s, m, n, eps, eval_integral) returns the Euler-Maclaurin approximation of a sum with m explicit terms and n correction terms, and an error bound. is_convergent() and is_absolutely_convergent() apply SymPy's convergence tests; they stop when no test decides.

Usage

sum_index(s, x)

reorder_limit(s, i, j)

sym_reorder(s, ...)

change_index(s, var, trafo, newvar = NULL)

reverse_order(s, ...)

euler_maclaurin(s, m = 0, n = 0, eps = 0, eval_integral = TRUE)

is_convergent(s)

is_absolutely_convergent(s)

continuous_domain(f, symbol, domain)

Arguments

s

A Sum or Product.

x, var

An index symbol.

i, j

Positions of limits, from 0.

...

Pairs (lists or vectors of two) of positions or indices, or positions or indices to reverse.

trafo

A linear expression in var.

newvar

The new index.

m, n

Numbers of explicit terms and of correction terms.

eps

Tolerance.

eval_integral

Evaluate the integral.

f

An expression.

symbol

The variable.

domain

A real set.

Value

An expression, a list or TRUE/FALSE.

Examples

n <- Symbol("n", integer = TRUE); a <- Symbol("a"); b <- Symbol("b")
x <- Symbol("x")
reverse_order(Sum(x * n, list(n, a, b)), 0)
#> Sum(-n*x, (n, b + 1, a - 1))
change_index(Sum(x^2, list(x, a, b)), x, x + 1)
#> Sum((x - 1)^2, (x, a + 1, b + 1))
is_convergent(Sum(1 / n^2, list(n, 1, oo)))
#> [1] TRUE
